ai.description: This gecko reaches 50–60 mm SVL. It is grey-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a distinctive row of enlarged, trihedral tubercles. It lacks a precloacal pore series and has undivided subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus yajurvedi* is best distinguished by its unique arrangement of enlarged, strongly keeled dorsal tubercles that are distinctly separated by smaller granular scales.
ai.habitat: The Kanker Rock Gecko inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops in central India, typically found at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kanker rock gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage on small insects while utilizing its specialized toe pads to navigate vertical rock surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus yajurvedi* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kanker rock gecko (*Hemidactylus yajurvedi*) is endemic to the Kanker district of Chhattisgarh, India, inhabiting rocky outcrops within the Deccan Plateau.
